name: Color picker
title: Color Picker: HEX, RGB, HSL, OKLCH and Contrast Checker
description: Pick a color and get HEX, RGB, HSL, CMYK and OKLCH values, tints and shades, and a WCAG contrast check. Pick from your screen or an image.
summary: HEX, RGB, HSL and OKLCH values, shades, and a WCAG contrast check.
howTo: Choose a color with the picker, type any CSS color (hex, RGB, HSL or a name like teal), pick one from your screen, or open an image and click on it.
Copy the value in the format you need: HEX for most tools, RGB or HSL for CSS, CMYK as a starting point for print, OKLCH for modern CSS.
Use the Contrast checker to test text against a background. It shows whether the pair passes WCAG AA and AAA, and suggests the nearest color that does.

faq.q: What contrast ratio do I need?
faq.a: WCAG 2.2 level AA asks for 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (24 px, or 19 px bold) and for buttons, icons and input borders. Level AAA asks for 7:1 and 4.5:1.

faq.q: How do I convert HEX to RGB?
faq.a: Split the six hex digits into three pairs and turn each from base 16 into a number: #ffc83d is ff, c8, 3d, which is rgb(255, 200, 61). Type either form above and every other format appears.
A newer way of writing colors, supported in modern CSS, where lightness matches how bright a color looks to people. It makes it easier to build palettes whose shades feel evenly spaced.

faq.q: Is the CMYK value exact for printing?
faq.a: No. It’s a straight mathematical conversion. Real print colors depend on the paper, ink and printer profile, so ask your printer for a proof of anything that has to match.
